key_insight: LLM agents can act as a natural-language layer for home energy scheduling, translating household preferences into practical appliance-control plans with near-optimal cost performance.
engineering_relevance: This work is relevant to device optimization because it shows how agentic AI can automate flexible-load scheduling against real tariff, weather, and solar signals while respecting household constraints.
method: ReAct tool-calling agent with live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, and household usage data.
Retrieval-augmented knowledge base plus MILP ground-truth scheduling for benchmark comparison.
Compared GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 under tariffs, conflicts, solar co-optimization, and week-long deployment.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark tests and a simulated week, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings, with projected annual savings of about GBP 1,270 versus an off-peak timer baseline.
watch_item: Results may be sensitive to integration reliability and constraint parsing, especially when using text-parsed actions instead of native function calling.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
